messages:
Renee: quick flag  ran bring-up for rankwise-1b int4 (mixed fp16 head, int4 body) on holdout-small+stat; saw NDCG_all -2.8 pts and MRR -0.03 absolute on the sampled holdout. interestingly the MRR drop is concentrated on short queries (<32 tokens).

Omar: can you paste the run args and the calibration set used for dynamic range? int4 is sensitive to calibration dist.

Renee: command:
```
./eval_rerank.py --model rankwise-1b --weights quant/mixed-int4.ckpt --holdout holdout-scan-2026-06 --seed 2026 --batch 256 --report ndcg,mrr --slice short
```
calib set: calib/sample-2k-random-2025 (used for dynamic range stats)

Vik: aha. calib/sample-2k-random-2025 is web-scraped longform heavy. if calibration expects longer context distribution, symmetric int4 scale can underrepresent short-query logits leading to rank compression.

Zoe: do you have baseline fp16 numbers for same seed + holdout?

EvalBot: run-summary: run=6180097777 model=rankwise-1b-int4 ndcg_all=0.603 ndcg_short=0.571 mrr_all=0.372 mrr_short=0.318 seed=2026 duration=38m

Renee: fp16 baseline -> ndcg_all=0.631 ndcg_short=0.599 mrr_all=0.402 mrr_short=0.349

Omar: so short-query mrr delta = -0.031 absolute (~8.9% relative). that's sizable. first reproducibility steps: 1) re-run int4 with calib set restricted to short-query-like examples (calib/short-2k), 2) compute bootstrap CI on mrr to see significance.

Vik: also run an ablation with per_layer_scale vs global_scale for int4. sometimes layerwise dynamic range helps preserve peak logits for short contexts.

Renee: kickstarting both: variant A = calib_short; variant B = layerwise_scales. ETA ~25m. will post quick stats.

EvalBot: run-started: 6180097783 variant=calib_short

EvalBot: run-started: 6180097785 variant=layerwise_scales

Renee: quick results: calib_short -> ndcg_all=0.622 ndcg_short=0.594 mrr_all=0.391 mrr_short=0.342; layerwise_scales -> ndcg_all=0.628 ndcg_short=0.597 mrr_all=0.398 mrr_short=0.347

Zoe: both helped. layerwise almost matches fp16 on short MRR. calibration choice looks important. please run a bootstrap significance test on short MRR with 10k resamples to confirm.

Omar: I'll run bootstrap script:
```
python -c "from stats import bootstrap_diff; print(bootstrap_diff('holdout-scan-2026-06','fp16','int4_layerwise','metric','mrr_short',n=10000))"
```

EvalBot: bootstrap-result: p_value=0.12 mean_delta=-0.002 se=0.008 (int4_layerwise vs fp16)

Vik: p=0.12 -> not statistically significant at 0.05. good sign. for calib_short variant: p_value=0.03 mean_delta=-0.007 se=0.006 (int4_calib_short vs fp16)

Zoe: interesting: layerwise_scales performs better and removes significance. recommendation: default int4 onboarding should use layerwise dynamic scaling with a calibration distribution that matches expected query length.

Renee: action items I'll add to bringup ticket: 1) require calibration dataset length match check (compute KL between calib token-length hist and holdout), 2) default to layerwise scales for int4, 3) include bootstrap significance test in validation harness. opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-evals/pull/501

Omar: also add a note in the onboarding doc to check model head precision (fp16 head) since head quantization often disproportionately affects MRR/top1.

Vik: let's add a CI threshold: if delta_mrr_short > 0.02 absolute and p<0.05, fail onboarding. Also log the calibration mismatch score.

EvalBot: created issue RNW-1955: add calib-parity-check + bootstrap gate. gist with layerwise vs global logit distributions: https://gist.github.com/eval/llogits-int4-layerwise

Renee: thanks all. will re-run full holdout with the layerwise default and attach artifacts to the onboarding ticket. closing thread.
